ask.text:
Every year the great sea turtles come up the beach at night to lay their eggs, and the village watches from the dunes in silence. This year one of the turtles is carrying something on her shell: a small woven basket, tied on with a strip of kelp. Out of the basket comes a thin, sleepy cry.
The elders say that long ago, a turtle carried the first child of the island to shore on her back, and that the turtles have never forgotten. The turtle is lumbering up the sand towards (subject)'s hiding place. Should (subject) untie the basket now, or wait until the turtle has laid her eggs?

c1o1.text: Inside the basket is a baby, damp and salty and very calm. The turtle waits until (subject) has lifted the basket clear, and then goes on up the beach as if nothing has happened. (subject) raises the turtle's child. Every year, on the night the turtles come, the child sits in the dunes beside (subject), and every year one old turtle stops and looks at them.

c1o2.text: (subject) lifts the basket off the turtle's shell and turns to find (subject.his/her) partner, (partner), right behind (subject.him/her), having followed (subject.him/her) out of the dunes. (partner) takes one look inside and says, "Well. We'd better go home." They raise the baby together, and name the sleeping basket "the shell."

c1.text: (subject) creeps out of the dunes and kneels beside the huge turtle, which stops and looks at (subject.him/her) with one old, wet eye. (subject.He/She) unties the kelp with trembling fingers...

c2o1.text: The turtle stops at the water's edge and lets (subject) untie the basket. The baby inside is asleep. The whole village, which has been watching from the dunes, comes running down to see, and the night of the turtles becomes the night of the turtle's child, celebrated every year after with a feast on the beach.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c2o2.text: (subject) is too slow. The turtle reaches the water, slips into the waves with the basket still on her back, and is gone. (subject) stands knee-deep in the surf, calling, until dawn. The elders say the turtle will find another beach, where somebody is quicker. (subject) is never late for the turtles again.

c2.text: (subject) stays still in the dunes while the turtle digs her nest, lays her eggs, and covers them. The cry from the basket goes quiet. When she turns to go back to the sea, (subject) runs down...
